references.text: The angel of the Lord promises Hagar that Ishmael's descendants will be so numerous they cannot be counted, an early promise of Ishmael's great future.
God assures Abraham that Ishmael will become a great nation because he is Abraham's offspring, even though the covenant is established through Isaac.
The fulfillment of God's promise: Ishmael's twelve sons are listed as twelve princes over their tribes, just as God promised in Genesis 17:20.
Similar wording (וְהִפְרֵיתִ֥י) where God promises Abraham fruitfulness and that kings will come from him, parallel to the promise concerning Ishmael.
Jacob receives the same covenant promises as Abraham, confirming that the promise of a great nation and eternal inheritance is passed down through the family line.
The promise to become a great nation given to Abraham in 12:2 is now specified and extended to also include Ishmael in 17:20.
The promise of numerous descendants and blessing for the nations repeats the core points of the covenant, which also apply to Ishmael.
The same covenant formula concerning kings and nations given to Abraham and Ishmael is now confirmed to Jacob.
Isaac's prayer that Jacob will become a congregation of peoples confirms the continuity of the covenant promise regarding multitude and nations.
17:20 is the direct extension of the promise in 17:4, where God's plan for 'a multitude of nations' is now specified for Ishmael.
The confirmation that Abraham will become a great nation in 18:18 highlights that Ishmael also receives a share of this promise to become a great nation.
Ishmael's twelve princes in 17:20 have a direct parallel to Jacob's twelve tribes in 49:28, showing a symmetrical structure in God's plan for both sons.
Jacob's prayer that his descendants will be numerous confirms that the promise of fruitfulness and multitude (given to Ishmael) applies to the entire family line.
The book of Hebrews confirms that the promise to make Abraham (and thus his lineage, including Ishmael) numerous is an eternal and unchanging covenant.
The promise to be as numerous as the stars in 22:17 confirms and expands upon the promise of multitude given to Ishmael in 17:20.
The creation word 'be fruitful' in 1:22 is the theological foundation for the promise of numerous descendants given to Ishmael in 17:20.
16:11 establishes Ishmael's birth and that God has heard, while 17:20 confirms his future destiny as a great nation with twelve princes.
Isaiah confirms that Abraham was made into many from one, which illuminates the promise that Ishmael will also become a great nation.
